title: US economy grew faster last quarter than initially reported | CNN Business
text:
Source: CNN

The US economy boomed last quarter, growing at an annualized rate of 4.3%, the Commerce Department reported on Wednesday. That’s a massive jump from the 3.4% rate initially reported. Both figures take inflation into account.

Business investment, boosted by software spending, was the single biggest driver of the third-quarter surge, a sign of major AI-related spending. Consumer spending, which accounts for three quarters of gross domestic product, also played a key role in delivering the best quarter of economic growth in three years.

But that robust growth comes with an inflation complication. In separate data released Wednesday, the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index — the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge — showed prices accelerated slightly to an annualized rate of 3.8% in October from 3.7% the prior month. That’s almost double the Fed’s target of 2%, solidifying the case for a rate hike next month.

On a monthly basis, price increases slowed to 0.3% from 0.5% in September.

The booming economy isn’t translating into increased wealth for many Americans, whose savings have dwindled as income growth has slowed.

While Wednesday’s PCE report showed that the personal savings rate (savings as a percentage of after-tax income) rose 0.5 percentage points to 4.1%, it’s below the 4.9% rate seen in October of last year. The increase in savings came from a boost in after-tax income growth last month, though much of that was tied to Medicare rebate payments.

But in a potentially worrisome sign for the economy, Americans are reining in their spending: When stripping out the 0.3% monthly price increase, spending was flat for October.

“The cautious consumer is back. It will be a bargain-hunting holiday for many Americans,” Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, wrote in a note Wednesday.

CNN’s Alicia Wallace contributed to this report.
